subject: Unexpected March charges — stacked prefetch / duplicate request IDs
messages:
From: Alyssa Smith <accounts-payable@orbitalretail.com>
To: Sergio Alvarez <sergio.alvarez@redwood.com>
Cc: ap@orbitalretail.com
Date: Wed, 28 Mar 2028 09:12:00 +0000
Subject: Unexpected March charges — prefetch batch double counts?

Hi Sergio,

Hope you’re well. We’ve reviewed our March invoice and see a large unexpected line item (~$9.2k) attributed to ‘prefetch/streaming tokens’ on several hourly windows. Our engineering team sampled a few request IDs and found duplicates across back-to-back batches — I’ve attached a short list (orbital_sample_requestids.txt) with three example request IDs and timestamps.

Quick asks:
- Can you provide the raw ingestion traces for the windows below (UTC): 2028-03-14 02:00–02:15, 2028-03-18 22:00–22:10, 2028-03-23 11:40–11:55?
- If this is a duplicate-counting issue on your side, we’ll need a provisional credit for the March invoice while you investigate.
- If it’s on our side (retries / client sending duplicates), we still need help with sampling and recommendations to avoid future hits.

Examples attached. We’re trying to close the month and would appreciate a response by EOD Friday.

Thanks —
Alyssa Smith
Senior Manager, Finance — Orbital Retail
accounts-payable@orbitalretail.com

[attachment: orbital_sample_requestids.txt (text, 3 lines)]

Subject: Re: Unexpected March charges — prefetch batch double counts?

Hi Alyssa — thanks for the examples and for flagging this so clearly. I’m looping in Ben from Billing and Kim from Platform to pull the requested traces and run a scan for duplicate request_id patterns across the windows you listed.

Immediate next steps from our side:
- Kim: can you pull the raw request traces and a token-count delta for the three windows (include request_id, timestamp, route, token_count)?
- Ben: please draft a provisional credit approach we can offer if we confirm an internal double-count.

Alyssa — I’ll follow up with a quick summary + provisional credit number within 24–48 hours. We can also provisionally stop charging for any confirmed duplicate request_ids while the investigation proceeds.

Appreciate the quick heads-up — we’ll prioritize.

Sergio Alvarez

Date: Thu, 29 Mar 2028 02:16:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Unexpected March charges — raw traces attached

Hi Alyssa / Sergio / Ben,

I pulled the traces for the three windows Alyssa flagged and attached a condensed CSV: usage_snapshot_march28.csv. Highlights from the preliminary forensic scan:
- We detect a repeating pattern where the same request_id appears in two neighbouring batches within a 30s–90s window in ~0.9% of requests for the specified windows.
- The route in question is the prefetch pipeline that backs up when clients retry without idempotency keys (our ingestion dedupe window is 30s by default).
- The duplicate occurrences show identical payload sizes and token counts — consistent with a client retry rather than an internal re-enqueue.

That said, there’s one case (request_id 7f9b1c...) where we see two separate ingestion events with the same request_id separated by 7 minutes; we’re investigating whether a backend retry/replay contributed.

Ben — provisional credit calc below (very conservative):
- Gross duplicate token count flagged: 1,840,120 tokens (sample extrapolated)
- Suggested provisional credit: $6,200 (covers flagged duplicates plus margin while we complete full audit)

Alyssa — please confirm whether Orbital wants the provisional credit applied to INV-2028-03-7789 while we finish the root cause analysis. If Orbital’s team can share their client retry logs for the same request IDs we can close faster.

Best,
Kimberly Park
Senior Platform Reliability Engineer — Redwood Inference
kimberly.park@redwood.com

[attachment: usage_snapshot_march28.csv (CSV, 120 rows condensed)]

From: Alyssa Smith <accounts-payable@orbitalretail.com>

Subject: Re: Unexpected March charges — provisional credit OK pending audit

Thanks Kim & team — this is helpful. We reviewed the CSV and agree to a provisional credit while you finish the audit. We’d like the credit applied to INV-2028-03-7789 now and will hold payment on the disputed amount pending the final RCA.

Two requests from our side:
1) Please provide a short formal credit note (line item and amount) so we can update our AP system.
2) Can you share the DocuSign link or confirmation text that will serve as mutual agreement for provisional credit (standard practice for our GPO).

If your investigation finds the root cause on our retry behavior, we agree to a postmortem and reversal of the provisional credit, but please flag that in writing up front.

Appreciate the quick turnaround.

— Alyssa

Date: Mon, 1 Apr 2028 16:30:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Unexpected March charges — provisional credit applied and next steps

Hi Alyssa — thanks for confirming.

Summary / actions taken:
- We applied a provisional credit of $6,200 to INV-2028-03-7789 (line item: "Provisional duplicate-token credit — review pending"). You should see the adjusted invoice at: https://app.redwood.com/invoices/INV-2028-03-7789/adjusted
- I’ve attached a one-page credit note (provisional-credit-note.pdf) and created a DocuSign envelope for mutual acknowledgement: https://docusign.redwood.com/envelopes/ENV-20280401-332 (expires in 14 days).
- Kimberly’s team will finish the full audit (expected EOD 2028-04-05) — deliverable will include full request_id tracebacks, recommended client-side idempotency settings, and any internal mitigation work we perform.

Mitigation recommendations (short):
- Add a client-side idempotency header (Idempotency-Key) when retrying requests.
- Increase our ingestion dedupe window to 120s for this route while we correlate with Orbital’s logs.
- We’ll schedule a 60-minute postmortem call the week of Apr 8 to review findings and next steps.

If Orbital is fine with the credit note and DocuSign, we’ll keep the provisional credit in place while we complete the RCA. If the audit attributes the duplicates to Orbital’s client retries, we will reverse the provisional credit (and provide full audit evidence).

Thanks again for the fast coordination — cc’ing Ben for invoice follow-through.

Sergio Alvarez
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
